description: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Evidence Catalogue indexing all 67 guideline PDF blocks with cancer site mapping, stage algorithms, Category 1/2A recommendations, concurrent systemic therapy indications, and radiation therapy principles.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Head and Neck Cancers

stage_algorithms.pathway: Surgical resection of primary +/- selective neck dissection (levels I-III). If adverse pathologic features (positive margins, extranodal extension), adjuvant chemoradiotherapy (Category 1). If close margins, perineural invasion, lymphovascular invasion, or pN1 without ENE, consider adjuvant RT alone.
Definitive radiation therapy alone (66-70 Gy) OR Transoral robotic surgery (TORS) with neck dissection. Adjuvant therapy de-intensification is investigational only.

stage_algorithms.stage: Oropharynx Locally Advanced (T3-4 or N+ p16-negative; or advanced p16-positive)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive concurrent chemoradiation with high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 IV every 3 weeks x 3 doses) (Category 1) OR induction chemotherapy followed by chemoradiotherapy.
Definitive radiation therapy alone (63 Gy in 28 fractions @ 2.25 Gy/fx or 66 Gy in 33 fractions @ 2 Gy/fx) OR transoral endoscopic laser resection (Category 1).

stage_algorithms.stage: Larynx Locally Advanced T2 bulky - T3 (Glottic / Supraglottic)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy with high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w) for organ preservation (RTOG 91-11) (Category 1) OR induction chemotherapy followed by RT/CRT OR total laryngectomy.
Concurrent chemoradiotherapy with cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w x 3) followed by adjuvant cisplatin/5-FU OR induction gemcitabine + cisplatin followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy (Category 1).

category_1_recommendations: Postoperative concurrent chemoradiation with high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w) for positive surgical margins and/or extranodal extension (ENE) (Category 1, based on EORTC 22931 and RTOG 9501).

Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy with high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w) for locally advanced squamous cell carcinoma of the larynx/hypopharynx/oropharynx for functional organ preservation (Category 1).
Definitive radiation therapy (66-70 Gy) or transoral surgery for early glottic and oropharyngeal carcinomas (Category 1).
Gemcitabine plus cisplatin induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemoradiotherapy for locoregionally advanced nasopharyngeal carcinoma (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: IMRT / VMAT is preferred for all definitive and postoperative head and neck radiotherapy to spare parotid, submandibular, swallowing, cochlear, and optic structures.
Weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2 IV weekly) as an alternative radiosensitizer for patients medically unfit for high-dose 3-weekly cisplatin.
Proton beam therapy (PBT) for base of skull, sinonasal tumors, or re-irradiation when normal tissue constraints cannot be met by photons.
Adjuvant RT alone (60-66 Gy) for pathological intermediate-risk features (pT3-T4, lymphovascular invasion, perineural invasion, >=2 positive nodes without ENE).
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: High-dose cisplatin 100 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 22, 43 is standard Category 1 concurrent systemic therapy. Indications: (1) Postoperative ENE or microscopically positive margins; (2) Definitive organ preservation for locally advanced stage III-IVB oropharynx, larynx, hypopharynx, and nasopharynx. Contraindications/modifications: GFR < 50-60 mL/min, pre-existing hearing loss/tinnitus, ECOG >= 2, or peripheral neuropathy require consideration of weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) or RT alone / cetuximab.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT/VMAT standard with daily IGRT. Simultaneous Integrated Boost (SIB) preferred.
radiation_therapy_principles.definitive_doses: Gross disease (primary and nodal GTV): 66-70 Gy (2.0-2.12 Gy/fx) in 33-35 fractions. High-risk subclinical regions: 60 Gy (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx). Low-to-intermediate risk elective nodal volumes: 50-54 Gy (1.6-1.8 Gy/fx).
radiation_therapy_principles.postoperative_doses: High risk (positive margins / ENE): 66 Gy (2.0 Gy/fx) with concurrent cisplatin. Intermediate risk: 60-66 Gy. Elective nodal bed: 50-54 Gy.

normal_tissue_constraints.parotid_glands: Mean dose < 26 Gy to at least one gland, or mean < 20 Gy to combined glands
normal_tissue_constraints.larynx_glottis: Mean dose < 35-45 Gy (when not target volume)

key_passages.text: IMRT is preferred in reducing long-term toxicity in oropharyngeal, nasal cavity, paranasal sinus, salivary gland, and nasopharyngeal cancers by reducing the dose to salivary glands, temporal lobes, auditory structures, and optic structures. SIB is commonly used in conventional (5 fractions/wk) and 6 fractions/wk accelerated schedules.

Gross disease coverage should typically be prioritized over these dose constraints for normal tissues, with the exception of neurologic OARs that are usually inviolable (ie, spinal cord, brainstem, optic structures). Mandible max <70 Gy, Brainstem D0.03cc 54-58 Gy, Spinal cord max 45 Gy (PRV 48 Gy), Parotid mean <26 Gy.
Adverse pathologic features: Extranodal extension +/- positive margin -> Systemic therapy/RT (category 1). Other risk features -> Consider RT.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer

stage_algorithms.stage: Stage IA-IB (T1a-c, T2a N0, medically inoperable or refusing surgery)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR / SBRT) is the standard definitive treatment (Category 1). Regimens: 48-60 Gy in 3-5 fractions for peripheral lesions, or 50-60 Gy in 5-8 fractions for central lesions ('no fly zone').

Neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (Nivolumab + platinum doublet x 3 cycles) followed by resection (CheckMate 816) OR surgery followed by adjuvant chemotherapy and osimertinib (for EGFR mut) or atezolizumab/pembrolizumab. Postoperative RT (PORT) is NOT routinely recommended for complete R0 resection pN2 (Lung ART / PORT-C), but indicated for positive margins (R1/R2) or extracapsular nodal extension.

Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (60-66 Gy in 30-33 fractions + cisplatin/etoposide or carboplatin/paclitaxel) followed by consolidation Durvalumab for up to 12 months in patients without disease progression (PACIFIC trial) (Category 1).
Local ablative therapy (SABR or surgical resection) to all metastatic sites and definitive thoracic treatment (chemoRT or SABR) in patients with controlled disease after initial systemic therapy.

category_1_recommendations: Definitive SABR/SBRT for medically inoperable early-stage Stage I (T1-T2aN0) NSCLC (Category 1).
Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (60-66 Gy in 30-33 fx with cisplatin/etoposide or carboplatin/paclitaxel) for inoperable Stage II-III locally advanced NSCLC (Category 1).

Consolidation Durvalumab immunotherapy (10 mg/kg q2w or 1500 mg q4w x 12 months) following definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy for unresectable Stage III NSCLC without disease progression (PACIFIC trial) (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: 4D-CT simulation with motion management (gating, abdominal compression, or internal target volume [ITV]) for lung radiotherapy planning.
FDG-PET/CT staging and radiation treatment planning to prevent geographic miss and spare uninvolved mediastinum.
Sequential chemotherapy followed by RT alone for patients medically unfit for concurrent chemoradiotherapy (poor PS, severe pulmonary disease).
Postoperative RT (54-60 Gy) for microscopic positive margins (R1) or extracapsular nodal extension.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy (Cisplatin + Etoposide OR Carboplatin + Paclitaxel OR Cisplatin + Pemetrexed [non-squamous only]) is indicated for all medically fit patients (ECOG 0-1, FEV1 >= 1.0 L, adequate renal/cardiac reserves) with unresectable Stage II/III disease. Radiation alone is reserved for patients with ECOG >= 2, severe weight loss (>10%), or major organ failure.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT/VMAT or 3D-CRT with 4D-CT motion management and daily IGRT.
radiation_therapy_principles.definitive_doses: Definitive concurrent chemoRT: 60-66 Gy at 2 Gy/fx in 30-33 daily fractions. Dose escalation above 70 Gy is detrimental (RTOG 0617).
radiation_therapy_principles.sabr_doses: Peripheral: 54 Gy in 3 fx (18 Gy/fx) or 50 Gy in 4-5 fx (10-12.5 Gy/fx) or 34 Gy single fraction. Central: 50-60 Gy in 5-8 fractions (6.25-10 Gy/fx).
radiation_therapy_principles.postoperative_doses: Negative margins (if indicated): 50-54 Gy. Extracapsular nodal extension / R1: 54-60 Gy. Gross residual: 60-70 Gy.

normal_tissue_constraints.spinal_cord: Max <= 50 Gy (conventional); SABR: 1 fx <= 14 Gy, 3 fx <= 18 Gy, 5 fx <= 30 Gy
normal_tissue_constraints.lungs_bilateral: V20 <= 35-40% (keep < 35% in elderly or taxane chemo); Mean Lung Dose (MLD) <= 20 Gy; V5 <= 65%
normal_tissue_constraints.heart: V40 <= 20%; Mean dose <= 20 Gy (RTOG 0617 showed heart dose strongly predicts OS)
normal_tissue_constraints.esophagus: Mean dose <= 34 Gy; Max <= 105% prescription; V60 <= 17%
normal_tissue_constraints.brachial_plexus: Median dose <= 69 Gy; SABR: 3 fx <= 24 Gy, 5 fx <= 32 Gy

key_passages.text: Commonly used doses for SABR: 25-34 Gy in 1 fx (peripheral small); 45-60 Gy in 3 fx (peripheral); 48-50 Gy in 4 fx (<4-5 cm); 50-55 Gy in 5 fx (central); 60-70 Gy in 8-10 fx (central).

Definitive RT with or without chemotherapy: 60-70 Gy, 2 Gy/fx, 6-7 weeks. Normal tissue constraints: Spinal cord max <=50 Gy; Lung V20 <=35%-40%, MLD <=20 Gy; Heart V40 <=20%, Mean <=20 Gy; Esophagus Mean <=34 Gy.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Prostate Cancer
subsites: Pelvic lymph nodes (obturator, internal/external iliac, presacral)

stage_algorithms.stage: Very Low and Low Risk (T1-T2a, PSA < 10, Grade Group 1)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Active Surveillance is preferred (Category 1). For patients refusing surveillance: EBRT monotherapy (moderate hypofractionation 60 Gy/20 fx or ultra-hypofractionated 36.25-40 Gy/5 fx) OR Low-Dose-Rate (LDR) brachytherapy (I-125 145 Gy or Pd-103 125 Gy) OR Radical Prostatectomy. NO ADT and NO elective nodal irradiation.

stage_algorithms.stage: Favorable Intermediate Risk (Grade Group 2, PSA 10-20, or T2b-c; <50% positive biopsy cores)
stage_algorithms.pathway: EBRT alone (hypofractionated or SBRT) OR Brachytherapy monotherapy (LDR or HDR) OR Active Surveillance in select low-volume cases. Routine ADT is NOT recommended.

stage_algorithms.stage: Unfavorable Intermediate Risk (Grade Group 3, or >=2 intermediate risk factors, or >=50% positive cores)
stage_algorithms.pathway: EBRT + Short-term ADT (4-6 months, Category 1) OR EBRT + Brachytherapy boost (LDR or HDR) +/- Short-term ADT (4-6 months).

stage_algorithms.stage: High and Very High Risk (Grade Group 4-5, PSA > 20, or cT3-T4)
stage_algorithms.pathway: EBRT + Long-term ADT (18-36 months, Category 1) OR EBRT + Brachytherapy boost + Long-term ADT (Category 1). For very high risk or node-positive: add Abiraterone acetate + prednisone for 2 years (STAMPEDE trial) (Category 1).

stage_algorithms.stage: Post-Radical Prostatectomy PSA Persistence / Biochemical Recurrence (BCR)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Early salvage radiation therapy (64-72 Gy) initiated at PSA 0.1-0.2 ng/mL + 6 months ADT (Category 1, SPPORT / GETUG-AFU 16 trials) +/- pelvic nodal RT.

category_1_recommendations: Active surveillance for very low and low-risk prostate cancer (Category 1).
Moderate hypofractionation EBRT (60 Gy in 20 fx or 70 Gy in 28 fx) as an efficacious and safe standard alternative to conventional fractionation (Category 1).
Short-term ADT (4-6 months) combined with definitive EBRT for unfavorable intermediate-risk prostate cancer (Category 1).
Long-term ADT (18-36 months) combined with definitive EBRT +/- brachytherapy boost for high-risk and very-high-risk localized prostate cancer (Category 1).
Addition of 2 years of Abiraterone acetate + prednisone to ADT + EBRT for very-high-risk / node-positive localized prostate cancer (Category 1, STAMPEDE).
category_2a_recommendations: Stereotactic Body Radiotherapy (SBRT / Ultra-hypofractionation: 36.25-40 Gy in 5 fractions) as a definitive monotherapy option for low and intermediate risk prostate cancer.
Brachytherapy boost (HDR 15 Gy in 1 fx or LDR I-125 108-110 Gy) combined with EBRT (45-50.4 Gy) for intermediate and high risk disease.
Elective pelvic nodal irradiation (45-50.4 Gy) for high-risk prostate cancer (POPART / RTOG trials).
PSMA-PET/CT staging prior to definitive or salvage therapy to exclude occult distant metastatic disease.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Androgen Deprivation Therapy (LHRH agonist/antagonist: Leuprolide, Goserelin, Degarelix, Relugolix) is indicated with RT: (1) Unfavorable intermediate risk: 4-6 months; (2) High/Very-high risk: 18-36 months (+ Abiraterone for 2 years if very-high risk); (3) Salvage RT: 6 months (+/- 24 months in high-risk salvage). ADT is contraindicated/unnecessary in Low Risk and Favorable Intermediate Risk.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT/VMAT with daily IGRT and fiducial markers / cone-beam CT. Hydrogel rectal spacer placement encouraged.
radiation_therapy_principles.definitive_doses: Conventional: 78-80 Gy in 39-40 fx (2.0 Gy/fx). Moderate hypofractionation: 60 Gy in 20 fx (3.0 Gy/fx) or 70 Gy in 28 fx (2.5 Gy/fx). SBRT: 36.25-40 Gy in 5 fractions (7.25-8.0 Gy/fx).
radiation_therapy_principles.brachytherapy: LDR monotherapy: I-125 145 Gy; Pd-103 125 Gy; Cs-131 115 Gy. LDR boost (with 45 Gy EBRT): I-125 108-110 Gy. HDR boost: 15 Gy in 1 fx or 19 Gy in 2 fx.
radiation_therapy_principles.salvage_doses: Prostatic bed: 64-72 Gy in 32-36 fx. Pelvic nodal bed (if indicated): 45-50.4 Gy.

normal_tissue_constraints.penile_bulb: Mean dose < 50 Gy to 95% of bulb

key_passages.text: Low Risk: Patients are encouraged to pursue active surveillance. Those electing treatment with RT may receive EBRT or brachytherapy as monotherapy. Patients should not be treated with ENI, ADT, or combination brachytherapy boost.
High Risk: Target should include prostate and seminal vesicles. RT options include EBRT or brachytherapy boost combined with EBRT. Combined with long-term ADT.

Neoadjuvant, Concurrent, and/or Adjuvant ADT with RT: Clinically localized high-risk or regional N1 disease: RT with LHRH agonist/antagonist plus antiandrogen; add abiraterone for 2 years in very-high-risk.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Rectal Cancer
subsites: Low rectum (<5 cm from anal verge)

stage_algorithms.pathway: Transabdominal resection (Total Mesorectal Excision [TME]: Low Anterior Resection or Abdominoperineal Resection). For favorable T1N0 (<3 cm, well/moderately differentiated, no LVI, negative margins): transanal local excision. NO neoadjuvant therapy required.

stage_algorithms.stage: Locally Advanced pMMR/MSS (cT3-4 N Any or cT1-2 N1-2, threatened MRF)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT) is preferred (Category 1). Options: (1) Long-course Chemoradiotherapy (50-50.4 Gy with capecitabine or 5-FU) followed by consolidation chemotherapy (FOLFOX or CAPEOX for 12-16 weeks) (OPRA regimen); (2) Induction chemotherapy followed by long-course Chemoradiotherapy (PRODIGE 23); (3) Short-course RT (25 Gy in 5 fractions) followed by consolidation chemotherapy (RAPIDO trial). Following TNT: Restaging with DRE, endoscopy, and pelvic MRI. If Clinical Complete Response (cCR): non-operative 'Watch-and-Wait' surveillance protocol (Category 2A). If residual disease: TME surgery.
Neoadjuvant immune checkpoint inhibition with Dostarlimab (PD-1 inhibitor) for 6 months (Cercek et al. NEJM 2022) or Pembrolizumab. Achieves >95% cCR rates, potentially omitting both CRT and surgery.

category_1_recommendations: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy (TNT) for locally advanced pMMR/MSS rectal cancer (cT3-T4 or node-positive) (Category 1, OPRA, PRODIGE 23, RAPIDO).
Fluoropyrimidine-based concurrent chemoradiation (50-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fx with capecitabine or infusional 5-FU) as neoadjuvant therapy (Category 1).
Short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week) followed by consolidation chemotherapy (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: Non-operative management ('Watch and Wait') for patients achieving a Clinical Complete Response (cCR) on digital rectal exam, flexible sigmoidoscopy, and high-resolution pelvic MRI after Total Neoadjuvant Therapy.
High-resolution baseline pelvic MRI with dedicated rectal cancer protocol to evaluate tumor depth, distance to Mesorectal Fascia (MRF), and extramural venous invasion (EMVI).
IMRT/VMAT for pelvic irradiation to spare small bowel, bladder, and femoral heads.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Oral Capecitabine (825 mg/m2 BID Monday-Friday on radiation days) or Continuous Infusion 5-FU (225 mg/m2/day 7 days/week) concurrent with long-course pelvic radiotherapy. Concurrent multi-agent regimens (oxaliplatin, irinotecan) add toxicity without improving locoregional control or survival and are NOT recommended concurrently with RT.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: 3D-CRT or IMRT/VMAT with full/comfortably full bladder and prone belly board or supine setup.
radiation_therapy_principles.long_course_doses: Pelvic target (primary tumor, mesorectum, presacral and internal iliac lymph nodes): 45 Gy in 25 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) followed by a boost to primary tumor and involved nodes to 50-50.4 Gy in 28 fractions.
radiation_therapy_principles.short_course_doses: 25 Gy in 5 daily fractions (5.0 Gy/fx) over 1 week, followed immediately by systemic chemotherapy.
radiation_therapy_principles.target_volumes: Gross primary tumor, mesorectum with safe margin, presacral space, internal iliac lymph nodes. For low rectal tumors invading sphincter or anterior organs, include external iliac and ischiorectal fossa.

normal_tissue_constraints.small_bowel: V45 < 195 cc (individual loops) or V45 < 65 cc (bowel bag), Dmax < 50 Gy

key_passages.section: REC-6 Clinical Stage T3, N Any; T1-2, N1-2
key_passages.text: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy: Long-course chemo/RT (Capecitabine or infusional 5-FU) or Short-course RT (25 Gy/5 fx) with consolidation chemotherapy (FOLFOX/CAPEOX 12-16 wk) followed by transabdominal resection or if complete clinical response, consider surveillance (REC-10A).
Radiation therapy is delivered with megavoltage photons (>=6 MV). 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions for long-course; 25 Gy in 5 fractions for short-course.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Cervical Cancer

stage_algorithms.pathway: Fertility-sparing (cone biopsy / trachelectomy) OR Radical Hysterectomy with pelvic lymphadenectomy (Category 1) OR definitive pelvic EBRT + brachytherapy for medically inoperable patients.

stage_algorithms.stage: Stage IB3 and IIA2 (FIGO 2018, bulky >=4 cm localized)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive Pelvic EBRT + Concurrent Platinum-containing Chemotherapy + Image-Guided Brachytherapy (IGBT) (Category 1). Radical hysterectomy is an alternative but carries high risk of dual modality morbidity.

stage_algorithms.stage: Stage IIB, III (IIIA-IIIC2), and IVA (Locally Advanced Cervical Cancer)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive Pelvic EBRT (plus extended field para-aortic RT if IIIC2 / positive para-aortic nodes) + Concurrent weekly Cisplatin (40 mg/m2) + Image-Guided Adaptive Brachytherapy (Category 1). Total point A / HR-CTV EQD2 target: >=80-85 Gy (>=85-90 Gy for larger residual tumors). INTERLACE protocol (induction carboplatin/paclitaxel followed by concurrent CRT) may be considered (Category 2A).

stage_algorithms.stage: Post-Hysterectomy Adjuvant Treatment (Peters Criteria - High Risk)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Positive pelvic lymph nodes, positive surgical margins, or positive parametrium: Adjuvant pelvic EBRT + concurrent cisplatin-containing chemotherapy (Category 1) +/- vaginal brachytherapy boost.

stage_algorithms.stage: Post-Hysterectomy Adjuvant Treatment (Sedlis Criteria - Intermediate Risk)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Negative nodes, negative margins, but meeting Sedlis criteria (deep stromal invasion, large tumor size >=4 cm, LVSI): Adjuvant pelvic EBRT alone (Category 1) +/- concurrent chemotherapy (Category 2B).

category_1_recommendations: Definitive Pelvic EBRT + Concurrent Platinum-based Chemotherapy + Brachytherapy for Stage IB3, IIA2, and Stage IIB-IVA locally advanced cervical cancer (Category 1).
Adjuvant pelvic EBRT + concurrent cisplatin-containing chemotherapy for high-risk surgical findings (positive nodes, margins, or parametrium) (Category 1, Peters trial).
Adjuvant pelvic EBRT alone for patients with negative nodes but meeting Sedlis criteria (Category 1, GOG 92).
Single-agent cisplatin (40 mg/m2 IV weekly, maximum 70 mg weekly) as the preferred concurrent radiosensitizer (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: Image-Guided Adaptive Brachytherapy (IGABT / IGBT) using MRI or CT at each insertion to delineate High-Risk CTV (HR-CTV), Intermediate-Risk CTV (IR-CTV), and bladder/rectum/sigmoid OARs.
Extended-field EBRT to cover common iliac and para-aortic lymph nodes when para-aortic nodal involvement is demonstrated on PET/CT or surgical staging (Category 2A).
Carboplatin as radiosensitizer for patients with renal impairment or neuropathy intolerant of cisplatin.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Weekly Cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV administered during EBRT (up to 5-6 doses). Indications: (1) Definitive treatment for FIGO IB3, IIA2, IIB, IIIA, IIIB, IIIC, IVA; (2) Adjuvant therapy for positive margins, nodes, or parametrium (Peters criteria).

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: Pelvic EBRT via IMRT/VMAT + 3D Image-Guided Brachytherapy (tandem & ovoids or tandem & ring +/- interstitial needles).
radiation_therapy_principles.ebrt_doses: Pelvic nodal bed and cervix: 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fx (1.8 Gy/fx). Parametrial or nodal boost: 5.4-10 Gy (total 54-60 Gy to involved nodes). Extended field para-aortic RT: 45 Gy.
radiation_therapy_principles.brachytherapy_doses: HDR brachytherapy: typically 28-30 Gy in 4-5 fractions (e.g. 7 Gy x 4 fx or 6 Gy x 5 fx). Cumulative HR-CTV D90 EQD2 must achieve >= 80-85 Gy (alpha/beta = 10).

key_passages.section: CERV-5 Stage IB3 and Stage IIA2
key_passages.text: Primary Treatment: Pelvic EBRT + concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy + brachytherapy (category 1).

Positive pelvic nodes, positive surgical margin, and/or positive parametrium: EBRT + concurrent platinum-containing chemotherapy (category 1) +/- brachytherapy. Sedlis criteria met: Pelvic EBRT (category 1).

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Anal Carcinoma
histologies: Squamous cell carcinoma (large cell nonkeratinizing, basaloid, cloacogenic)

stage_algorithms.stage: Stage I (T1, N0, M0 - Anal Canal)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy with 5-FU + Mitomycin C + RT (Nigro regimen) (Category 1). For highly selected superficial perianal / anal margin T1N0: local excision with 1 cm margin (if sphincter preservation intact).

stage_algorithms.stage: Stage II-III (T2-T4, N0 or Any T, N1-N3, M0)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (Nigro regimen: Mitomycin C + 5-FU or Capecitabine + RT) (Category 1). Dose: 50.4-54 Gy to gross primary and nodal disease, 45 Gy to elective pelvic and bilateral inguinal nodal basins. Abdominoperineal Resection (APR) is reserved STRICTLY for persistent or recurrent disease (salvage APR).
Systemic chemotherapy with Carboplatin + Paclitaxel (preferred, EA2165) OR modified DCF (docetaxel, cisplatin, 5-FU). Palliative RT to symptomatic pelvic primary or bone metastases.

category_1_recommendations: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy with 5-FU and Mitomycin C (Nigro regimen) for localized anal canal squamous cell carcinoma (Category 1, ACT I, RTOG 87-04, RTOG 98-11).

Cisplatin is NOT equivalent to Mitomycin C: RTOG 98-11 established that Mitomycin C provides superior colostomy-free survival and disease-free survival compared to cisplatin in definitive CRT (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: Oral Capecitabine (825 mg/m2 BID on radiation days) as an acceptable substitute for continuous infusion 5-FU in combination with Mitomycin C (Category 2A).
IMRT / VMAT is preferred to reduce severe acute skin desquamation, gastrointestinal, and genitourinary toxicity.
Mandatory elective bilateral inguinal lymph node irradiation in all stages II-III disease (45 Gy in 25 fractions).
Post-treatment digital rectal exam and anoscopy evaluation delayed until 12-26 weeks post-CRT to allow complete delayed regression before declaring failure.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Nigro regimen: 5-FU (1000 mg/m2/day continuous IV days 1-4 and 29-32) + Mitomycin C (10 mg/m2 IV bolus days 1 and 29, max 20 mg per dose). Alternatively, Capecitabine (825 mg/m2 BID on RT days) + Mitomycin C (10 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 29). Single-modality radiation alone has significantly inferior local control and higher colostomy rates and is restricted only to patients completely unfit for chemotherapy.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT / VMAT standard. SIB technique widely utilized.
radiation_therapy_principles.doses: T1-T2 N0: 50.4 Gy to gross tumor in 28 fx (1.8 Gy/fx). T3-T4 or node positive: 54 Gy in 30 fx (1.8 Gy/fx). Elective pelvis and bilateral groins: 45 Gy in 25 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx).
radiation_therapy_principles.target_volumes: Anal canal GTV, mesorectum, presacral nodes, internal and external iliac nodes, and bilateral superficial/deep inguinal lymph nodes.

key_passages.text: IMRT is preferred to reduce acute toxicity and treatment breaks. Total dose to gross disease: 50.4-54 Gy; elective nodal regions including bilateral inguinal nodes: 45 Gy.

5-FU 1000 mg/m2/day continuous infusion days 1-4 and 29-32 with Mitomycin 10 mg/m2 IV bolus days 1 and 29 (capped at 20 mg). Capecitabine 825 mg/m2 BID on RT days is an acceptable substitute for 5-FU.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Esophageal and Esophagogastric Junction Cancers

stage_algorithms.stage: Locally Advanced Resectable SCC (cT1b-T4a, N Any)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy (CROSS regimen: 41.4 Gy with weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin) followed by esophagectomy OR Definitive chemoradiotherapy (50-50.4 Gy) for cervical esophagus or organ preservation (Category 1). If residual pathologic disease after trimodality therapy: adjuvant Nivolumab for 1 year (CheckMate 577) (Category 1).

stage_algorithms.stage: Locally Advanced Resectable Adenocarcinoma (cT1b-T4a, N Any)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy (CROSS: 41.4 Gy with weekly paclitaxel/carboplatin, Category 1) followed by esophagectomy OR Perioperative chemotherapy (FLOT regimen: 4 cycles pre-op, 4 cycles post-op, Category 1). If trimodality resection reveals residual pathologic disease (ypT+ or ypN+): adjuvant Nivolumab for 1 year (Category 1, CheckMate 577).

stage_algorithms.stage: Locally Advanced Unresectable or Medically Inoperable
stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy to 50-50.4 Gy with paclitaxel/carboplatin or fluoropyrimidine/oxaliplatin (Category 1).

category_1_recommendations: Preoperative chemoradiotherapy with paclitaxel + carboplatin (CROSS regimen) for resectable locally advanced esophageal and EGJ cancers (Category 1).
Definitive chemoradiotherapy (50-50.4 Gy) for patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma desiring organ preservation or cervical esophagus location (Category 1).

Adjuvant Nivolumab immunotherapy for 1 year in patients with residual pathologic disease (ypT+ or ypN+) following neoadjuvant chemoradiation and complete R0 surgical resection (Category 1, CheckMate 577).
Perioperative FLOT chemotherapy for resectable EGJ adenocarcinoma (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: IMRT / VMAT preferred to minimize cardiopulmonary toxicities (radiation pneumonitis, cardiac mortality).
Proton beam therapy (PBT) considered to spare lung and heart in lower esophageal and EGJ tumors.
Restaging FDG-PET/CT post-neoadjuvant therapy to assess metabolic response and rule out interval metastasis.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: CROSS regimen: Paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 + Carboplatin AUC 2 IV weekly on days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 concurrent with radiation. Alternative: Fluorouracil (or Capecitabine) + Oxaliplatin (FOLFOX). Radiotherapy alone is reserved only for palliative symptom relief (dysphagia, bleeding) in patients unfit for systemic therapy.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT / VMAT with 4D-CT simulation and IV contrast. Proton therapy in select cases.
radiation_therapy_principles.preoperative_doses: 41.4-50.4 Gy in 23-28 fractions (1.8 Gy/fx) (41.4 Gy in 23 fx per CROSS protocol).
radiation_therapy_principles.definitive_doses: 50.0-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx). Doses >50.4 Gy do not improve survival (INT 0123).
radiation_therapy_principles.postoperative_doses: 45.0-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fractions for positive margins.
radiation_therapy_principles.target_volumes: GTV (primary + involved nodes). CTV: primary tumor + 3-4 cm expansion superior/inferior along esophagus, 1 cm radial expansion. Nodal CTV: 0.5-1.5 cm around involved nodes plus elective drainage stations (celiac for lower, supraclavicular for upper).

key_passages.text: Preoperative RT: 41.4-50.4 Gy (1.8-2.0 Gy/day) (total 23-28 fractions). Definitive RT: 50-50.4 Gy (1.8-2.0 Gy/day) (total 25-28 fractions). Postoperative RT: 45-50.4 Gy.
Lungs: V20 <= 20%, V10 <= 40%, Mean < 20 Gy. Spinal Cord: Max <= 45 Gy. Heart: V30 <= 30%. Kidneys: V20 <= 33%.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Bladder Cancer

stage_algorithms.stage: Non-Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer (NMIBC: Ta, T1, Tis)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Complete TURBT followed by intravesical therapy (BCG induction and maintenance for high risk; intravesical gemcitabine or mitomycin for intermediate/low risk). Radical cystectomy for BCG-unresponsive disease.

stage_algorithms.stage: Muscle-Invasive Bladder Cancer (cT2-T4a, N0, M0 - Trimodality Candidate)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Trimodality Bladder-Preservation Therapy: Maximal aggressive TURBT followed by Concurrent Chemoradiotherapy (Category 1). Patient criteria: solitary tumor, complete TURBT, no extensive Tis/CIS, normal renal function, no hydronephrosis. Mid-treatment cystoscopic assessment at 40-45 Gy: if complete response, complete CRT to 64-66 Gy. If persistent invasive tumor: prompt radical cystectomy.
Neoadjuvant Cisplatin-based Chemotherapy (Gemcitabine + Cisplatin or ddMVAC) followed by Radical Cystectomy + bilateral pelvic lymphadenectomy (Category 1).

category_1_recommendations: Trimodality bladder preservation combining maximal TURBT with concurrent chemoradiotherapy for muscle-invasive bladder cancer (Category 1).
Neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy prior to radical cystectomy for cT2-T4aN0 disease (Category 1).
Cisplatin + 5-FU OR 5-FU + Mitomycin C (BC2001 regimen) as radiosensitizers in bladder preservation (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: Weekly Cisplatin (35-40 mg/m2) as concurrent radiosensitizer for bladder preservation.
Adaptive radiotherapy planning (Plan-of-the-day / library of plans) to manage daily internal organ motion from varying bladder filling.
Prompt salvage radical cystectomy in patients failing to achieve clinical complete response on mid-treatment or post-treatment restaging cystoscopy.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Chemotherapy radiosensitization is REQUIRED for curative-intent bladder preservation. Regimens: (1) Cisplatin (20 mg/m2/day days 1-2 and 15-16) + 5-FU (500 mg/m2/day continuous infusion); (2) 5-FU (500 mg/m2/day continuous days 1-5 and 16-20) + Mitomycin C (12 mg/m2 day 1) (BC2001 trial); (3) Weekly Cisplatin 35-40 mg/m2. RT alone is inferior and reserved for palliative haematuria control or medically frail patients.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: IMRT / VMAT with daily IGRT and empty bladder protocol (or reproducible bladder volume).
radiation_therapy_principles.doses: Whole bladder +/- pelvic lymph nodes: 40-45 Gy in 20-25 fractions (1.8-2.0 Gy/fx). Tumor bed boost: 20-24 Gy to total 64-66 Gy.
radiation_therapy_principles.target_volumes: GTV (prior tumor bed from pre-TURBT imaging), whole bladder CTV, pelvic lymph nodes (obturator, internal and external iliac) up to common iliac bifurcation.

key_passages.text: Definitive concurrent chemoradiation following maximal TURBT (Category 1) is an established bladder-sparing alternative to radical cystectomy in select patients.
Bladder-preserving concurrent CRT: 64-66 Gy total dose with radiosensitizing chemotherapy (cisplatin/fluorouracil, 5-FU/mitomycin C, or weekly cisplatin).

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer

stage_algorithms.stage: Early Stage Invasive (T1-T2, N0) after Breast-Conserving Surgery (BCS)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Whole Breast Irradiation (WBI) with moderate hypofractionation (40-42.5 Gy in 15-16 fractions) is standard (Category 1). Boost to tumor bed (10-16 Gy) indicated for age <=50, high grade, or close/focal positive margins. Accelerated Partial Breast Irradiation (APBI: 26-30 Gy in 5 fx or 34 Gy BID in 10 fx) is an acceptable alternative for low-risk women >=50, ER+, negative margins >=2 mm. Omission of RT may be considered in women >=65-70 years with T1N0 ER+ tumors receiving endocrine therapy (CALGB 9343, PRIME II).

stage_algorithms.stage: Locally Advanced / Node-Positive (>=4 positive nodes, or T3-T4)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Post-Mastectomy Radiation Therapy (PMRT) to chest wall and regional lymph nodes (supraclavicular, infraclavicular, axillary levels I-III, internal mammary) (Category 1). For 1-3 positive nodes: PMRT strongly recommended for high-risk features (grade 3, LVI, age <40, close margins, large tumor size) (Category 1).

Trimodal therapy: Neoadjuvant systemic chemotherapy (taxane/anthracycline +/- anti-HER2) followed by Modified Radical Mastectomy followed by Post-Mastectomy Radiation Therapy (PMRT: 50 Gy + boost to 60-66 Gy) (Category 1). Immediate reconstruction is contraindicated.

category_1_recommendations: Moderate hypofractionated Whole Breast Irradiation (40-42.5 Gy in 15-16 fx) as preferred standard over conventional fractionation (Category 1).
Post-Mastectomy Radiation Therapy for patients with >=4 positive axillary lymph nodes or T3/T4 primary tumors (Category 1).
Regional Nodal Irradiation (RNI: supraclavicular and internal mammary nodes) for patients with high-risk node-positive disease (Category 1, MA.20 and EORTC 22922).
category_2a_recommendations: Ultra-hypofractionated whole breast RT (26 Gy in 5 fractions over 1 week, FAST-Forward trial) as an acceptable treatment option.
Deep Inspiration Breath Hold (DIBH) technique for left-sided breast cancer to minimize cardiac dose and late ischemic heart disease.
Axillary radiation as an alternative to axillary lymph node dissection in patients with positive sentinel lymph nodes meeting ACOSOG Z0011 or AMAROS criteria.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Sequential administration is standard: Adjuvant chemotherapy precedes radiation therapy. Trastuzumab, Pertuzumab, and endocrine therapy (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitors) may be given concurrently with radiation therapy. Anthracyclines must NEVER be administered concurrently with RT due to severe cardiotoxicity and recall pneumonitis.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: 3D-CRT, Field-in-Field, or IMRT/VMAT with DIBH gating for left breast.
radiation_therapy_principles.wbi_doses: Moderate hypofractionation: 40 Gy in 15 fx (2.67 Gy/fx) or 42.5 Gy in 16 fx (2.66 Gy/fx). Conventional: 45-50.4 Gy in 25-28 fx. FAST-Forward: 26 Gy in 5 fractions. Tumor bed boost: 10-16 Gy in 4-8 fx.
radiation_therapy_principles.pmrt_doses: Chest wall + RNI: 40-42.5 Gy in 15-16 fx or 50 Gy in 25 fx (+ 10-16 Gy scar boost if positive margin).

normal_tissue_constraints.heart: Left breast DIBH: Mean heart dose < 1-2 Gy; V20 < 5%; LAD Dmax < 20 Gy

key_passages.text: Hypofractionated whole breast irradiation (40 Gy in 15 fractions or 42.5 Gy in 16 fractions) is preferred. Regional nodal irradiation includes supraclavicular/infraclavicular nodes, internal mammary nodes, and axillary nodes when indicated.
PMRT recommended for >=4 positive nodes (category 1), T3/T4 tumors, and 1-3 positive nodes with high-risk features.

entries.title: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Central Nervous System Cancers

stage_algorithms.pathway: Maximal safe surgical resection followed by Standard Radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions) + concurrent Temozolomide (75 mg/m2 daily) followed by 6 cycles of adjuvant Temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2 x 5 days/28 days) + Alternating Electric Field Therapy (TTFields / Optune) (Category 1, Stupp protocol and EF-14 trial).

Hypofractionated Radiotherapy (40 Gy in 15 fractions or 34 Gy in 10 fractions) + concurrent and adjuvant Temozolomide (Category 1 for MGMT-methylated, Perry trial). If MGMT unmethylated and poor KPS: hypofractionated RT alone or best supportive care.

stage_algorithms.stage: IDH-mutant High-Risk Grade 2-3 Astrocytoma or Oligodendroglioma
stage_algorithms.pathway: Maximal safe resection followed by RT (54 Gy in 30 fx for grade 2; 59.4-60 Gy for grade 3) followed by PCV chemotherapy (procarbazine, CCNU, vincristine) (Category 1, RTOG 9802 and CATNON / EORTC 26951) OR Temozolomide.

stage_algorithms.stage: Brain Metastases (1-4 lesions, controlled systemic disease)
stage_algorithms.pathway: Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS / SRT: 18-24 Gy in 1 fraction or 24-27 Gy in 3 fractions) preferred over Whole Brain RT to preserve cognitive function and memory (Category 1).

category_1_recommendations: Standard RT (60 Gy in 30 fx) + concurrent daily Temozolomide (75 mg/m2) and adjuvant Temozolomide (150-200 mg/m2) for newly diagnosed glioblastoma in good PS patients (Category 1, Stupp et al.).
Addition of Alternating Electric Field Therapy (TTFields) to adjuvant Temozolomide for glioblastoma (Category 1, EF-14 trial).
Hypofractionated RT (40 Gy in 15 fx) + Temozolomide for elderly/frail glioblastoma patients with methylated MGMT promoter (Category 1, Perry et al.).
Adjuvant PCV chemotherapy following radiotherapy for high-risk low-grade glioma (Category 1, RTOG 9802).
Stereotactic Radiosurgery (SRS) alone for limited brain metastases (1-4 metastases) to avoid neurocognitive decline associated with WBRT (Category 1).
category_2a_recommendations: Hippocampal avoidance whole brain radiotherapy (HA-WBRT) with Memantine to reduce neurocognitive toxicity when WBRT is required.
Lomustine (CCNU) + Temozolomide combined with RT for MGMT-methylated glioblastoma in young patients (CeTeG trial, Category 2B).
Advanced MRI fusion (T1 contrast, FLAIR, perfusion, MR spectroscopy) for GTV and CTV definition.
entries.concurrent_systemic_indications: Temozolomide 75 mg/m2 PO daily given continuously from day 1 of RT to the last day of RT (42 days) with Pneumocystis jirovecii prophylaxis (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole). Essential in glioblastoma; synergistic radiosensitization.

radiation_therapy_principles.technique: 3D-CRT or IMRT/VMAT; SRS using Gamma Knife, CyberKnife, or Linac-based cone/multi-leaf collimator.
radiation_therapy_principles.doses: Glioblastoma: 60 Gy in 30 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx). Low-grade glioma: 45-54 Gy in 1.8 Gy/fx. Anaplastic glioma / Grade 3: 59.4-60 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy/fx. SRS for Brain Mets: <=2 cm: 24 Gy; 2.1-3 cm: 18 Gy; 3.1-4 cm: 15 Gy.
radiation_therapy_principles.target_volumes: Glioblastoma GTV: surgical cavity + residual T1-contrast enhancing lesion. CTV: GTV + 1.5-2.0 cm margin adjusted for anatomic boundaries (falx, skull, ventricles).

normal_tissue_constraints.retina_lens: Lens Dmax < 6-10 Gy, Retina Dmax < 45 Gy

key_passages.text: Good PS (KPS >= 60), Age <= 70: Standard RT + concurrent Temozolomide and adjuvant Temozolomide + alternating electric field therapy (Category 1) or Standard RT + concurrent and adjuvant Temozolomide (Category 1).
Adult High-Grade Infiltrative Astrocytomas: 60 Gy in 30 fractions (2.0 Gy/fx). Elderly/poor PS: 40 Gy in 15 fractions or 34 Gy in 10 fractions.

entries.title: Radiation Therapy for Oropharyngeal Squamous Cell Carcinoma: An ASTRO Clinical Practice Guideline

stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive IMRT/VMAT alone (70 Gy in 35 fractions or 66 Gy moderately accelerated) or definitive concurrent CRT. De-intensification is currently recommended only in clinical trial settings.
Definitive concurrent chemoradiation with high-dose cisplatin (100 mg/m2 q3w, minimum target cumulative dose 200 mg/m2) using bilateral neck IMRT.

category_1_recommendations: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy (70 Gy at 2 Gy/fraction over 7 weeks with concurrent high-dose cisplatin) strongly recommended for locally advanced oropharyngeal carcinoma (cT3-T4 or cN1-N3).
Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy (IMRT) with daily image guidance (IGRT) is mandatory to minimize xerostomia and dysphagia while maintaining locoregional control.
category_2a_recommendations: Elective nodal irradiation (50-54 Gy in 1.8-2.0 Gy/fx) recommended for bilateral levels II-IV and retrostyloid space when nodal risk exceeds 15-20%.
concurrent_systemic_indications: High-dose cisplatin 100 mg/m2 every 3 weeks (days 1, 22, 43) preferred over weekly cisplatin (40 mg/m2) for definitive curative intent, unless renal/hearing comorbidities mandate adjustment.
radiation_therapy_principles: Prescription dose: High-risk CTV 70 Gy (2.0 Gy/fraction); Intermediate/Subclinical risk CTV 60 Gy; Elective nodal CTV 54-56 Gy.
Constrictor muscle mean dose < 50 Gy and contralateral parotid mean dose < 26 Gy strongly prioritized.

key_passages.text: For patients with locally advanced oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma receiving definitive radiation, concurrent platinum-based chemotherapy is strongly recommended over radiation alone.

IMRT or VMAT should be utilized for all patients treated with curative-intent radiation for oropharyngeal carcinoma to spare salivary glands and swallowing apparatus without compromising tumor control.

entries.title: ESTRO-ACROP Consensus Guideline on Target Volume Delineation and Radiotherapy in Head and Neck Cancer
entries.organization: European Society for Radiotherapy and Oncology (ESTRO)

stage_algorithms.pathway: Comprehensive bilateral elective neck delineation (levels Ib-IV +/- V) with simultaneous integrated boost (SIB) up to 70 Gy with concurrent cisplatin.

category_1_recommendations: Delineate primary GTV on contrast-enhanced CT co-registered with MRI/PET; CTV margin 5-10 mm trimmed at natural anatomic barriers (bone, deep fascia).
category_2a_recommendations: Level II-IV elective coverage indicated for tonsillar carcinoma even in cN0 disease due to high rate (>20%) of occult micro-metastases.
concurrent_systemic_indications: Concurrent cisplatin radiosensitization indicated for all T3-T4 or node-positive squamous cell carcinomas with WHO performance status 0-1.
radiation_therapy_principles: SIB technique: PTV_high 69.96-70 Gy (2.12 Gy/fx), PTV_low 54-56 Gy (1.64-1.7 Gy/fx) in 33 fractions.
Swallowing-sparing IMRT (pharyngeal constrictors mean < 50 Gy) significantly improves 2-year dysphagia-free survival.

key_passages.text: Elective neck nodal delineation must adhere to standardized consensus boundaries. In unilateral tonsillar tumors with < 1 cm soft palate extension and cN0-N1, contralateral elective neck irradiation may be tailored under strict multidisciplinary criteria.

entries.title: JASTRO / FARO Guidelines for Radiotherapy of Head and Neck Cancers
entries.organization: Japanese Society for Radiation Oncology (JASTRO) & Federation of Asian Organizations for Radiation Oncology (FARO)

stage_algorithms.pathway: Definitive chemoradiotherapy using weekly cisplatin (30-40 mg/m2) or tri-weekly cisplatin (80-100 mg/m2) tailored to Asian population body surface area and tolerability.

category_1_recommendations: Definitive high-precision IMRT/VMAT (70 Gy in 35 fractions) combined with platinum chemotherapy remains standard organ preservation approach.
category_2a_recommendations: Weekly low-dose cisplatin (40 mg/m2/week for 6-7 doses) demonstrates comparable locoregional control with reduced acute nephrotoxicity in Asian patient cohorts.
concurrent_systemic_indications: Systemic chemotherapy indicated for T2-T4 with nodal positivity; strict pre-hydration and creatinine clearance monitoring >= 50 mL/min required.
radiation_therapy_principles: Organ at risk constraints: Parotid contralateral mean < 26 Gy, Oral cavity mean < 30 Gy, Mandible Dmax < 66 Gy to prevent osteoradionecrosis.

key_passages.text: In Asian clinical practice, weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m2 during definitive radiotherapy is well validated and accepted as an effective alternative to tri-weekly high-dose cisplatin, ensuring higher full-dose compliance.

entries.title: AROI Consensus Guidelines on Radiotherapy in Head and Neck Cancers
entries.organization: Association of Radiation Oncologists of India (AROI)

stage_algorithms.pathway: Concurrent chemoradiotherapy (70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks with concurrent Cisplatin 30-40 mg/m2 weekly or 100 mg/m2 tri-weekly). Pre-treatment dental evaluation, prophylactic PEG tube assessment, and nutritional intervention are mandatory.

category_1_recommendations: Definitive concurrent chemoradiotherapy is the primary standard of care for locally advanced unresected oropharynx cancer.
All patients must undergo comprehensive clinical oral examination and extraction of unsalvageable teeth at least 10-14 days prior to commencing radiotherapy to prevent osteoradionecrosis.
category_2a_recommendations: Weekly cisplatin 30-40 mg/m2 is pragmatic, highly concordant with Indian patient tolerance, and provides equivalent locoregional control when cumulative dose >= 200 mg/m2 is attained.
concurrent_systemic_indications: Concurrent cisplatin is indicated for all locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinomas with ECOG PS 0-2 and GFR >= 50 mL/min.
radiation_therapy_principles: Target volumes: CTV-P (Primary) 70 Gy in 35 fractions, CTV-N (Involved nodes) 70 Gy, CTV-Elective (Uninvolved nodal stations) 50-54 Gy.
Spinal cord PRV max < 48 Gy; Mandible max < 70 Gy; Bilateral submandibular and parotid sparing prioritized.

key_passages.text: Given high prevalence of tobacco and betel nut etiology in the subcontinent, rigorous mucosal toxicity monitoring, early speech/swallowing therapy, and nutritional supplementation are essential components of curative-intent chemoradiation.

entries.title: American Brachytherapy Society (ABS) Consensus Guidelines for Head and Neck Brachytherapy

stage_algorithms.stage: Early stage primary or localized recurrence
stage_algorithms.pathway: Interstitial high-dose-rate (HDR) or low-dose-rate (LDR) brachytherapy as boost (15-20 Gy) following external beam RT (45-50 Gy), or definitive monotherapy (40-45 Gy HDR) in selected superficial/accessible oral tongue/tonsillar pillar lesions.

category_1_recommendations: Interstitial brachytherapy boost provides superior local dose escalation with steep dose fall-off, sparing superficial bone and contralateral salivary glands.
category_2a_recommendations: Catheter spacing 1.0-1.2 cm using Paris system geometry; mandible lead shielding recommended when implants approach the gingivobuccal sulcus.
concurrent_systemic_indications: Chemotherapy usually withheld during interstitial catheter placement and active brachytherapy delivery to avoid severe mucosal dehiscence.
radiation_therapy_principles: HDR fraction size typically 3-4 Gy twice daily with minimum 6-hour interval between fractions.

key_passages.text: For accessible oropharyngeal and oral cavity malignancies, interstitial brachytherapy delivers highly localized conformal dose escalation while minimizing radiation exposure to pharyngeal constrictors and spinal cord.
